articles.title: Augusto Cury apoia Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno: 'Iremos cobrar' | G1
articles.standfirst: Escritor de Ribeirão Preto (SP) foi o terceiro mais votado no primeiro turno das eleições 2026. Ele disse que o senador aceitou suas propostas e assinou um compromisso público.
articles.summary: Augusto Cury apoia Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno das Eleições 2026 após o senador assinar um compromisso público com as propostas do escritor.
articles.body:
O ex-candidato à Presidência da República Augusto Cury (Avante) afirmou nesta quinta-feira (8) nas redes sociais que o apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da corrida presidencial das eleições 2026 contra o atual presidente Lula (PT) não é um cheque em branco ao senador.

O escritor de Ribeirão Preto (SP), terceiro mais votado no primeiro turno, disse que tomou a decisão depois que Flávio o "ouviu de maneira profunda e inteligente", aceitou as propostas apresentadas e assinou um compromisso público.

"Neste segundo turno, decidi dar um voto de confiança a Flávio Bolsonaro , que está reivindicando o seu primeiro mandato e depois fim da reeleição. Mas deixo claro não é um cheque em branco, é um compromisso comigo e com o Brasil. Eu e todo o povo brasileiro iremos cobrar", afirmou.

O ex-candidato à presidência da República, Augusto Cury (Avante) — Foto: Redes sociais

Flávio Bolsonaro recebeu mais de 56 milhões de votos e enfrentará, no segundo turno, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, candidato do PT à reeleição, que recebeu 53,8 milhões de votos. Flávio recebeu 47,03% dos votos válidos; Lula ficou com 45,15%. O segundo turno está marcado para 25 de outubro.

Com mais de três milhões de votos no primeiro turno e críticas aos candidatos do PL e do PT durante a campanha , Cury inicialmente chegou a dizer que não apoiaria ninguém na segunda etapa da eleição, mas na quarta-feira (7) foi às redes sociais para explicar seu silêncio, prometendo que se pronunciaria em breve.

Nesta quinta-feira, após uma conversa por telefone com Flávio, Cury confirmou oficialmente seu suporte à campanha do senador na reta final do pleito.

"Desde o primeiro turno, escolhi o silêncio, porque há tempo de falar e tempo de calar. E as grandes decisões não nascem do barulho, mas da reflexão e da consciência", afirmou, em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais.

Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, diz que aposentadorias ficarão fora do corte de gastos — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Quais compromissos foram aceitos por Flávio?

Augusto Cury afirmou que Flávio Bolsonaro se comprometeu com diferentes projetos e ideias apresentadas pelo escritor depois de uma longa conversa "olho no olho".

"Não pedi cargos, nem influência. Exigi apenas um compromisso de entregar um Brasil melhor para cada brasileiro. E ele me ouviu de maneira profunda e inteligente. Flávio aceitou minhas propostas e assinou um compromisso público comigo e com o Brasil."

Segundo uma carta de compromissos divulgada pelo ex-candidato e assinada pelo senador, Flávio assumiu que vai trabalhar para as seguintes pautas sugeridas por Cury:

Fim da reeleição presidencial , com defesa da alternância de poder e da renovação democrática;

Transformação da saúde , com ampliação da telemedicina e do acesso à medicina moderna;

Proteção integral às mulheres , com uso de tecnologia e enfrentamento da violência;

Transformação da educação , com valorização dos professores e melhores salários;

Financiamento de até dez milhões de microempresas , para estimular o empreendedorismo e a geração de empregos;

Fortalecimento do cooperativismo , com defesa do ato cooperativo, apoio às cooperativas e verticalização agroindustrial;

Valorização da agricultura , com a meta de dobrar a produção sustentável de alimentos em dez anos;

Pacificação nacional , com um governo para todos os brasileiros, independentemente de suas convicções políticas, e combate à corrupção.

"Quanto a Flávio Bolsonaro, fui exigente. Afirmei que precisamos de um governo para todos, sem ódio, sem vingança. Fiz perguntas e apresentei várias propostas", afirmou Cury.

Nas redes sociais, o escritor também explicou, por outro lado, que não apoia Lula por discordar do projeto de governo dele, além de ser contra a reeleição. "Não é pessoal, é por causa do projeto."

articles.title: Oktoberfest de Igrejinha: tudo o que você precisa saber sobre a festa | G1
articles.standfirst: 37ª acontece no Parque de Eventos Almiro Grings. Resultados financeiros são revertidos para projetos e entidades locais, totalizando R$ 37 milhões desde a criação.
articles.summary: 37ª acontece no Parque de Eventos Almiro Grings. Resultados financeiros são revertidos para projetos e entidades locais, totalizando R$ 37 milhões desde a criação.
articles.body:
Oktoberfest de Igrejinha, no RS — Foto: Divulgação/ Cleiton Miguel

A 37ª Oktoberfest de Igrejinha começa nesta sexta-feira (9) e promete transformar o Parque de Eventos Almiro Grings em um grande encontro de música, cultura alemã, gastronomia e tradição. Ao longo de dez dias, até 18 de outubro, a festa reúne mais de 80 atrações, cerca de 150 apresentações e nove palcos espalhados pelo complexo .

Por trás dos shows, dos desfiles, dos espaços temáticos e dos milhares de litros de chopp servidos ao público, está uma força-tarefa formada por mais de 3,5 mil voluntários . Eles são responsáveis por organizar a estrutura do evento, considerado a maior festa comunitária do Brasil.

Segundo a presidente da 37ª edição, Aline Hess, o modelo da Oktoberfest de Igrejinha é único. Além de ser organizada pela própria comunidade, a festa reverte os resultados financeiros para projetos e entidades da região .

Desde a criação do evento, mais de R$ 37 milhões já foram destinados a iniciativas nas áreas de saúde, segurança, educação e cultura .

A expectativa da organização é ultrapassar a marca de 200 mil visitantes nesta edição . De acordo com a presidente, já há ingressos vendidos para turistas de todos os estados brasileiros e também para visitantes de outros países.

Quem passar pela Oktoberfest neste ano encontrará mudanças em diferentes áreas do evento. Uma das principais novidades é o Pavilhão da Cerveja , chamado de Bierhalle , que ocupa o espaço do antigo ginásio.

O ambiente contará com mesas de confraternização, chopes especiais e pilsen servidos em copos de vidro, gastronomia inspirada na culinária alemã, climatização e decoração com referências bávaras.

A Lona de Encontro, agora chamada de Treffzelt, também foi remodelada e passa a oferecer novas opções gastronômicas, bebidas e apresentações musicais.

A programação terá nomes de diferentes estilos musicais. Entre os destaques estão Simone Mendes, Di Ferrero, Turma do Pagode, Traia Véia, Guilherme & Benuto, Acústicos & Valvulados, Alok e a banda alemã voXXclub .

A abertura oficial ocorre na sexta-feira, com cerimônia na Bierhalle. Mais tarde, Simone Mendes encerra a primeira noite no palco principal.

No sábado (10), o tradicional desfile da Oktoberfest percorre ruas da cidade antes das atividades no parque. À noite, Di Ferrero é a principal atração.

Já no domingo (11), a programação inclui atrações culturais durante a tarde, seguida pelos shows de Turma do Pagode e Traia Véia.

No encerramento, em 18 de outubro, a banda alemã voXXclub sobe ao palco no fim da tarde. Na sequência, Alok fecha a programação principal com um espetáculo que reúne música, luzes e drones.

Os ingressos para a Oktoberfest de Igrejinha estão à venda no site oficial da festa e são válidos para um único dia de programação. No primeiro lote, os valores variam entre R$ 27 e R$ 48, conforme a data da visita.

articles.title: Médica suspensa por mensagem sobre petistas: hospital nega atrasos | G1
articles.standfirst: Maternidade Célia Câmara informou que a apuração interna ainda está em andamento. Defesa esclareceu que a médica não foi demitida, mas teve o contrato suspenso temporariamente.
articles.summary: A Maternidade Célia Câmara investiga médica suspensa por mensagem sobre petistas e afirma que nenhum paciente teve a liberação atrasada durante as eleições.
articles.body:
A Maternidade Célia Câmara, em Goiânia , informou que nenhuma alta médica foi adiada após uma médica orientar colegas a não liberarem pacientes petistas durante as eleições. Segundo a unidade, a apuração interna ainda está em andamento, mas já foi possível constatar que nenhum paciente teve a alta postergada em razão da mensagem.

“A apuração ainda está em curso, mas já se sabe que nenhuma alta foi adiada”, informou a maternidade.

A médica Marcella Segato de Sousa Melo teve o contrato suspenso temporariamente após a repercussão de uma mensagem enviada a um grupo de WhatsApp de profissionais da unidade. No texto, ela orientou que os colegas não dessem alta a pacientes durante o fim de semana da votação e fez referência à preferência política deles.

Em nota, a defesa da profissional esclareceu que ela não foi demitida e que a suspensão do contrato permanece em vigor enquanto são realizados os procedimentos internos.

“A profissional não foi formalmente demitida. O contrato da médica foi suspenso temporariamente, enquanto são realizadas as apurações internas”, informou a defesa.

Médica é suspeita de orientar funcionários a ‘não dar alta para petistas’ em dia de eleição — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhaguera

A mensagem foi enviada em um grupo de WhatsApp de médicos da maternidade na sexta-feira (2), antes do primeiro turno das eleições. Na publicação, Marcella escreveu: “Quem estiver na enfermaria sábado e domingo, não dar alta para ninguém, a maioria é petista”.

O conteúdo repercutiu após a divulgação de uma captura de tela da conversa. A orientação foi denunciada ao Ministério Público Federal (MPF), e o caso também chegou à Procuradoria Regional Eleitoral em Goiás, que encaminhou a situação ao órgão do Ministério Público Eleitoral com atribuição para apuração.

A Procuradoria informou ainda que adotou medidas preventivas para garantir o livre exercício do voto no segundo turno. Os detalhes dos procedimentos não foram divulgados devido à restrição de acesso às informações.

Hospital e Maternidade Municipal Célia Câmara (HMMCC), no Conjunto Vera Cruz, em Goiânia, Goiás — Foto: Diomício Gomes/O Popular

A defesa destacou que a suspensão temporária do contrato não significa o encerramento do vínculo profissional com a maternidade.

“A suspensão temporária não se confunde com a rescisão contratual. É necessário aguardar a conclusão dos procedimentos internos para qualquer posicionamento definitivo sobre o vínculo profissional”, afirmou.

Em manifestação anterior, Marcella pediu desculpas pela mensagem e afirmou que nenhuma decisão médica foi tomada com base na preferência política dos pacientes. A profissional também declarou que nenhuma alta foi negada ou atrasada por esse motivo.

articles.title: Quem é atleta paralímpica que amputou perna após câncer e 12 cirurgias | G1
articles.standfirst: Natural de Venda Nova do Imigrante, jogadora da Seleção Brasileira de vôlei sentado, conquistou bronze em Tóquio e ouro no Mundial da Bósnia; fora das quadras, compartilha viagens, treinos e momentos da vida pessoal.
articles.summary: Natural de Venda Nova do Imigrante, jogadora da Seleção Brasileira de vôlei sentado, conquistou medalhas; fora das quadras, compartilha viagens, treinos e momentos da vida pessoal.
articles.body:
Natural de Venda Nova do Imigrante, na Região Serrana do Espírito Santo, Luiza Fiorese construiu no esporte uma nova trajetória depois de enfrentar um câncer ainda na adolescência. Aos 15 anos, a capixaba foi diagnosticada com um osteossarcoma no fêmur esquerdo e precisou substituir parte dos ossos da perna por uma endoprótese.

Antes do diagnóstico, Luiza praticava handebol. O tratamento, porém, fez com que ela precisasse deixar o esporte. Anos depois, uma oportunidade inesperada abriu um novo caminho para a capixaba.

Em novembro de 2018, uma jogadora da Seleção Brasileira de vôlei sentado viu Luiza em um programa de televisão e entrou em contato com ela. Naquele período, a atleta já havia passado por duas cirurgias. Em março de 2019, aceitou o convite para conhecer a modalidade.

A experiência deu início à carreira de Luiza no esporte paralímpico. Desde então, ela passou a integrar a Seleção Brasileira de vôlei sentado e conquistou importantes resultados internacionais.

Entre os títulos da capixaba estão a medalha de bronze nos Jogos Paralímpicos de Tóquio 2020 e o ouro no Mundial da Bósnia, em 2022.

Rainha da 38ª Festa da Polenta, Luiza Fiorese — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Luiza Fiorese/Facebook

Fora das quadras, Luiza também compartilha com os seguidores momentos da rotina. Nas redes sociais, a atleta costuma mostrar os exercícios físicos e a preparação para as competições, além de registrar viagens e momentos da vida pessoal.

Apaixonada por viagens, ela também vive uma nova fase fora do esporte. No início deste ano, Luiza ficou noiva.

A atleta nasceu em julho de 1997 e, além da carreira esportiva, é formada em Jornalismo. Luiza Fiorese também foi coroada rainha da 38ª Festa da Polenta em Venda Nova do Imigrante, em 2016.

Após passar por 12 cirurgias desde a adolescência, a atleta paralímpica Luiza Fiorese decidiu amputar a perna e iniciar uma nova fase da vida. A jogadora de vôlei sentado recebeu alta no domingo (4) e contou, com exclusividade ao g1 , como tem sido a adaptação após o procedimento.

Medalha de ouro no Mundial da Bósnia, em 2022, e bronze nos Jogos Paralímpicos de Tóquio 2020, Luiza passou por uma amputação transfemoral, realizada logo acima do joelho. No final de setembro, Luiza publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais contando sobre o que a levou a tomar essa decisão.

Para ela, a cirurgia representa o fim de um ciclo marcado por procedimentos médicos e o começo de uma rotina com mais liberdade e qualidade de vida.

Luiza Fiorese, paratleta de vôlei sentado do Brasil, decidiu amputar a perna após passar por diversas cirurgias — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A história de Luiza com os procedimentos médicos começou aos 15 anos, quando ela foi diagnosticada com um osteossarcoma, tumor que atinge os ossos . No caso dela, o câncer foi encontrado no fêmur , o maior osso do corpo humano, localizado na coxa.

Após o tratamento, parte do fêmur esquerdo da atleta precisou ser substituída por uma endoprótese, um implante cirúrgico usado para substituir parte ou a totalidade de um osso.

Em junho deste ano, Luiza passaria por uma nova troca da endoprótese. O implante antigo foi retirado e um espaçador foi colocado no local para preparar a cirurgia.

Durante esse período, porém, o espaçador se quebrou enquanto a atleta se movimentava na cama. O problema provocou dores e novas complicações.

Foi quando o médico apresentou duas possibilidades à paciente: colocar uma nova endoprótese, que precisaria ser substituída novamente cerca de dez anos depois, ou realizar a amputação, que poderia ser a última cirurgia da vida dela.

Luiza contou que a possibilidade de passar novamente por anos de procedimentos fez com que ela refletisse sobre a vida que desejava ter no futuro. A decisão foi tomada após conversar com a família, o noivo, amigos e médicos.

Médico conseguiu preservar parte da perna

A jogadora de vôlei explicou que, como o osso da coxa era muito curto, a amputação normalmente seria realizada na altura do quadril.

O médico, porém, aproveitou a parte saudável dos ossos abaixo do joelho. Eles foram reposicionados e unidos à parte restante do fêmur com uma placa, permitindo que a amputação ficasse mais próxima do joelho.

A recuperação e a adaptação ainda estão no início. Mesmo assim, Luiza já percebe mudanças positivas na rotina. Antes da cirurgia, ela estava andando com a ajuda de muletas havia três meses. Segundo a atleta, as atividades do dia a dia ficaram mais fáceis depois da amputação.

Quem é Luiza Fiorese, atleta paralímpica do Espírito Santo que amputou a perna após câncer e 12 cirurgias — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Para Luiza, a amputação não representa uma perda. Ela afirmou que o procedimento trouxe a possibilidade de recuperar a liberdade. A possibilidade da amputação já havia sido pensada anteriormente, mas a atleta disse que foi importante ela se preparar psicologicamente e amadurecer primeiro.

"Eu não vejo a amputação como uma coisa que me tirou algo. Eu vejo como algo que me deu liberdade de viver de novo", disse.

A atleta também defende que a amputação seja tratada com mais naturalidade e que as necessidades das pessoas com deficiência sejam consideradas, inclusive os impactos emocionais, familiares e financeiros e o alto custo das próteses.

"A vida não para com amputação. Falo disso no lugar da menina de 15 anos que teve que colocar uma endoprótese. Minha vida não parou ali, só se multiplicou. Conquistei coisas que jamais imaginei conquistar", relembrou.

Luiza passou pelo procedimento em São Paulo, mas pretende concluir a reabilitação perto dos pais e dos cachorros, no sítio da família em São Roque, comunidade rural de Venda Nova do Imigrante, no Sul do Espírito Santo.

Os primeiros objetivos são recuperar a mobilidade, andar bem e voltar a ter qualidade de vida. Depois, Luiza quer viajar. Ela contou que precisou cancelar diversos passeios por causa das cirurgias e das complicações. Agora, pretende conhecer novos destinos ao lado da família e das amigas.

Atleta paralímpica do ES, Luiza Fiorese, decide amputar perna após 12 cirurgias: 'Liberdade de viver de novo' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Uma das mudanças que já espera experimentar é durante as viagens de avião. Como não conseguia dobrar o joelho, tinha dificuldade para se acomodar nos assentos.

"Eu tô doida para ver como vai ser entrar num avião agora que eu posso sentar reto numa cadeira e só ir", contou, animada.

Luiza também contou com o apoio do noivo, Gabriel Garcia, que também é atleta. Ele a pediu em casamento em fevereiro deste ano. Segundo a atleta, Gabriel ajudou a dar segurança para que ela tomasse a decisão pensando no próprio bem-estar.

articles.title: Peste bubônica: a doença da Idade Média que ainda faz vítimas | G1
articles.standfirst: Responsável por matar 60% da população europeia na Idade Média, peste é rara hoje em dia, mas continua circulando em algumas regiões do mundo e, sem diagnóstico e tratamento rápidos, pode ser fatal.
articles.summary: A peste bubônica, causada pela bactéria Yersinia pestis, ainda circula no mundo e exige diagnóstico rápido para evitar que sintomas fatais sejam confundidos com uma gripe.
articles.body:
Pulgas são vetores da peste bubônica — Foto: John Montenieri/CDC/BSIP/picture alliance

Os primeiros sintomas que Paul Gaylord percebeu foram semelhantes aos de uma gripe. Dois dias antes, ele havia sido mordido por seu gato, que parecia visivelmente doente. Os médicos lhe receitaram antibióticos contra a doença da arranhadura do gato, uma infecção bacteriana que pode surgir após arranhões ou mordidas de felinos.

Mas os medicamentos não funcionaram. O estado de Gaylord piorou, ele foi internado na UTI e acabou entrando em coma. Não estava com gripe nem com a doença da arranhadura do gato: havia contraído a peste, uma enfermidade que normalmente associamos à Idade Média, e não à vida contemporânea no estado americano de Óregon.

Os sintomas vagos e a raridade da doença dificultam o diagnóstico, mas a peste ainda existe e não perdeu seu potencial letal. Gaylord sobreviveu por pouco e contou sua história ao jornal britânico The Guardian em 2014.

A peste é causada pela bactéria Yersinia pestis. Ela pode entrar no organismo humano por diferentes vias e se multiplicar rapidamente. A bactéria danifica tecidos em diversos órgãos, provoca hemorragias e, sem tratamento, leva à morte em quase 100% dos casos.

A forma mais comum é a peste bubônica, também chamada de peste negra. Nesse caso, as pulgas atuam como vetores . Ao picarem um roedor infectado por Yersinia pestis, podem transmitir a bactéria para humanos. O microrganismo se multiplica nos gânglios linfáticos, que incham de forma dolorosa.

Se o agente causador entrar diretamente na corrente sanguínea, por exemplo por meio da mordida de um mamífero infectado, pode ocorrer uma peste septicêmica, uma grave infecção do sangue.

Já na peste pneumônica, o patógeno chega aos pulmões por gotículas ou aerossóis emitidos por um animal ou uma pessoa infectada. Essa é a única forma da doença em que a transmissão direta entre seres humanos é considerada provável.

Segundo o Instituto Robert Koch, órgão responsável pelo controle de doenças na Alemanha, são registrados até 3 mil casos de peste por ano em todo o mundo.

Hoje, as regiões mais afetadas são a República Democrática do Congo, o Uganda e, principalmente, Madagáscar, onde ocorreu o último grande surto, em 2017. No país africano, entre 250 e 500 pessoas são infectadas anualmente. Casos também continuam surgindo ocasionalmente no oeste dos Estados Unidos.

Na Idade Média, porém, a situação era muito diferente. Entre 1347 e 1353, a peste matou cerca de 25 milhões de pessoas. A doença deu origem a uma pandemia que durou aproximadamente 500 anos e eliminou cerca de 60% da população europeia.

Ainda assim, a bactéria não começou a infectar seres humanos na Idade Média. Arqueólogos encontraram vestígios de Yersinia pestis em esqueletos com mais de 5.500 anos. Um estudo recente concluiu que a bactéria provavelmente é letal para humanos há muito mais tempo do que se imaginava.

O arqueólogo e bioquímico Ben Krause-Kyora, da Universidade de Kiel, na Alemanha, estuda a interação entre patógenos antigos e o sistema imunológico humano.

Segundo ele, uma das questões mais fascinantes é entender quais fatores de virulência permitiram que a peste deixasse de ser apenas uma doença de roedores para se transformar numa pandemia devastadora para os seres humanos.

Pesquisas mostram que as variantes mais antigas da bactéria não possuíam os genes necessários para a transmissão por vetores como as pulgas. É possível que, naquela época, a infecção ocorresse por outros meios, inclusive pelo consumo de roedores contaminados.

No final da Idade do Bronze ocorreu uma mudança decisiva: a bactéria desenvolveu o chamado gene ymt, que permitiu sua transmissão por pulgas. A partir daí, o patógeno passou por uma transformação rápida e profunda, abrindo caminho para os grandes surtos e pandemias.

Apesar das epidemias devastadoras do passado, a peste desapareceu da Europa após 1945, quando os últimos casos foram registrados na ilha francesa da Córsega.

Segundo o biólogo molecular Holger Scholz, chefe do Laboratório Nacional de Referência para Yersinia pestis do Instituto Robert Koch, a principal razão é que hoje não há, em geral, roedores infectados circulando dentro das casas europeias.

Na Idade Média, residências eram compartilhadas por pessoas e ratos, criando condições ideais para que as pulgas transmitissem a bactéria aos humanos.

Além disso, os ratos não costumam ser reservatórios ideais da doença, pois frequentemente adoecem e morrem. Já algumas espécies de roedores em outras regiões do mundo desenvolveram certa resistência e servem de reservatório natural para a bactéria.

Scholz e sua equipe trabalham com parceiros em áreas onde a doença continua endêmica, incluindo Madagáscar. Um dos objetivos é melhorar a infraestrutura laboratorial para acelerar o diagnóstico da peste.

Isso é fundamental porque a identificação precoce da doença continua sendo um dos maiores desafios. Scholz relata o caso de um jovem corredor nos Estados Unidos que foi mandado para casa com um diagnóstico de gripe. Ele morreu porque ninguém suspeitou que pudesse ser peste.

O problema é que os primeiros pacientes de um surto frequentemente morrem antes que o diagnóstico correto seja estabelecido e o tratamento seja iniciado.

Embora existam antibióticos eficazes contra a doença, em alguns lugares eles demoram dias para chegar aos pacientes. Esse atraso pode ser fatal, sobretudo nos casos de peste pneumônica, que pode matar em até 48 horas após o início dos sintomas.

A peste pode voltar a causar uma pandemia?

Apesar dos surtos ocasionais, Scholz considera extremamente improvável que a peste provoque uma nova pandemia mundial.

A bactéria não é transmitida com a mesma facilidade que vírus, como o da gripe ou o Sars-Cov-2, causador da covid-19. Além disso, hoje existem recursos de combate muito mais eficazes do que na Idade Média, incluindo antibióticos e padrões modernos de higiene.

Um cenário mais preocupante seria o uso da bactéria como arma biológica após manipulação genética. Por isso, especialistas monitoram continuamente as diferentes cepas de Yersinia pestis. Técnicas modernas de análise genética permitem identificar a origem das amostras e até verificar se houve manipulação laboratorial.

Embora seja teoricamente possível que viajantes tragam a doença de volta à Europa, os especialistas consideram essa possibilidade extremamente remota. Ainda assim, a vigilância permanece essencial para evitar que casos isolados se transformem em surtos maiores.

articles.title: Margaret Hamilton, scientist who worked on Nasa's Apollo programme, dies
articles.summary: American scientist Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the computer system used by Nasa's Apollo lunar program, has died at the age of 90, her
articles.body: American scientist Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the computer system used by Nasa's Apollo lunar program, has died at the age of 90, her former employer said Wednesday. In a statement, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology called Hamilton, who taught at the university from 1959 to the mid-1970s, a "computing pioneer" and said she died on Sept 30."To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer - to say she was ahead of her time - would be an understatement," said Olivier de Weck, the Apollo Program Professor and interim head of the MIT department of aeronautics and astronautics. "She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved," de Weck added.The famed Apollo programme allowed US to beat the Soviet Union in the race to become the first humans to land on the Moon. Nasa chief Jared Isaacman paid tribute to Hamilton on X, calling her "a pioneer whose work helped make Apollo and humanity's first journeys to the moon possible."Born in Indiana in 1936, Hamilton studied mathematics before moving to Boston, Massachusetts with her husband in 1959. She found employment at MIT, working in meteorology before she joined a lab in 1965 that was seeking people to develop software to "send a man to the Moon."Hamilton "was hired as the first programmer for the Apollo project at MIT, as well as the first female programmer in the project," the university said. "By 1968, she was assistant director in charge of (Apollo's) Command and Service Module team, and more than 400 people were working on Apollo's software," MIT said.Hamilton was credited with making critical onboard systems more robust and accident-resistant. Her software intervened approximately three minutes before the Eagle lander of the Apollo 11 mission touched down on the Moon, overriding a faulty script and ensuring the mission could safely continue, according to Nasa.Jerry Wohletz, CEO of the Draper Laboratory - which was spun out of the MIT Instrumentation Lab - said Hamilton left "an indelible mark" on the company. "Through her leadership and contributions to the development of the onboard flight software for Nasa's Apollo Guidance Computer, she helped ensure that Apollo astronauts landed safely on the lunar surface and safely returned home," he said.Hamilton was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by former president Barack Obama in 2016 for her achievements. Hamilton went on to publish more than 130 papers and started her own software companies Higher Order Software and Hamilton Technologies.(BY AFP)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: California is set to become the first US state to ban popular kitchen countertops made with engineered stone, Australia did the same in 2024; 'fear' is growing ...
articles.summary: America's third-largest state California is reportedly on track to enact the country's first ban on engineered quartz countertops.
articles.body: America's third-largest state California is reportedly on track to enact the country's first ban on engineered quartz countertops. According to a report in USA Today, the upcoming ban is in response to an alarming rise in Silicosis, a debilitating lung disease, in people who work with the material. Over the past decade, engineered quartz has reportedly dominated American kitchen and bathroom renovations, as it is an affordable, durable, and low-maintenance alternative to natural marble and granite. However, that commercial boom has coincided with an occupational health crisis. Australia enacted a nationwide complete ban on engineered stones in 2024.Engineered stones, also called artificial stone or quartz countertops, are man-made stone countertops designed to look like natural stone. According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), engineered stone is manufactured by binding 90% to 95% crushed quartz with resins, polymers, and pigments. When workers cut, grind, drill, sand, or polish these slabs, the process generates high concentrations of respirable crystalline silica dust. Inhaling these microscopic particles causes progressive, irreversible scarring of lung tissue.Why California wants to ban countertops made of engineered stonesCalifornia has emerged as an epicenter of the crisis, home to a large concentration of fabrication shops and an escalating caseload among stone cutters. The state, where several quartz countertop manufacturers and fabricators are based, has seen a notable rise in cases of lung diseases.In a recent report, the California Department of Public Health estimated that 662 silicosis cases, including 35 deaths and 75 cases resulting in lung transplants, have been diagnosed among quartz manufacturers and workers in the state since 2019. In the petition, the California Division of Occupational Safety and Health, or Cal/OSHA, called the cluster of silicosis cases a "crisis." It said, "California is experiencing a rapidly worsening silicosis crisis among artificial stone workers, driven by dangerous materials and regulatory shortcomings."California’s petition wants to follow Australian modelThe petition also mentions Australia banning these engineered stones. It said, "Australia faced a comparable crisis and, after finding that enforcement alone was ineffective, implemented a nationwide prohibition of artificial stone containing more than 1% crystalline silica in July 2024. The ban succeeded: safer alternatives replaced artificial stone without reported job losses or significant consumer impact, and enforcement became dramatically simpler. Prohibiting fabrication and installation of artificial stone in California could substantially mitigate silicosis risk while simplifying enforcement. There is, however, an important caveat — Australia controls the entire supply chain (imports, manufacture, and sale), whereas Cal/OSHA can only regulate sites of employment (such as locations where fabrication and installation occurs). If artificial stone remains commercially available in California, some non-compliant shops may go underground, concentrating risk in the least regulated settings."You use AI every day. articles.title: 'ICE out of our neighbourhoods’: Shooting of Dominican man sparks protests in New York
articles.summary: An ICE agent shot and wounded a Dominican man during an arrest in New York City on Thursday, triggering protests and drawing sharp criticism from local
articles.body: An ICE agent shot and wounded a Dominican man during an arrest in New York City on Thursday, triggering protests and drawing sharp criticism from local leaders over the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.The shooting took place in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of Manhattan, near the Bronx, during what the department of homeland security (DHS) described as a “targeted enforcement operation”. The man survived and was being treated at a hospital, the agency said, but it did not explain what led the officer to open fire.According to preliminary information cited by CNN, agents from Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) Enforcement and Removal Operations branch encountered a person they were targeting shortly after 4 pm. DHS said agents were attempting to arrest a Dominican man with a prior criminal conviction and a history of other arrests when an officer discharged his weapon.Early reporting also indicated that there was a five-year-old child in the same car. The child was physically unharmed, mayor Mamdani shared later in a statement.The agency described the man as a “criminal illegal alien”, saying he had a previous conviction for grand larceny. It said New York police had arrested him in December 2023 before he was released, blaming what it called “reckless sanctuary policies” in Democrat-led cities. DHS did not provide further details about the circumstances of Thursday’s shooting.The incident sparked anger among New York officials and residents, with demonstrators gathering at the scene and chanting, “ICE off our streets now!”Mamdani slams ICE Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting “unconscionable and incredibly serious” and said he had called president Donald Trump over the incident. Mamdani later said he would demand an end to ICE enforcement operations in the city. A spokesperson for the mayor said Trump and Mamdani had not spoken as of Thursday evening.“Our thoughts are with the injured New Yorker and his family tonight. We are praying for his recovery,” Mamdani said. “Get ICE out of our neighborhoods.”New York governor Kathy Hochul, who said she had been briefed on the shooting, called on federal authorities to explain what happened.“We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding this incident. New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why,” she said.DHS defended its enforcement operations, saying officers were often required to make arrests in public spaces and unpredictable, dangerous environments when people it considers dangerous are released from custody. The department said its agents provided immediate aid to the injured man.The New York police department said its officers were not involved in the shooting. It called for a mobilisation after the incident to manage crowds and handle evidence at the scene.Witnesses share details of shooting Witnesses described hearing several gunshots. Pedro Almaraz, who works at a nearby restaurant, told AP that he heard about three or four shots and saw a man on the ground surrounded by officers wearing face masks and vests marked with Department of Homeland Security branding.Videos and photographs shared on social media showed a man sitting on the ground with his hands behind his back after the shooting. Another video appeared to show New York police officers lifting an injured man and carrying him into a police vehicle. A damaged car was also seen blocking the road, with small holes in two of its windows.The presence of armed federal officers also raised concerns among some residents about their identification. Alfred Silva, 38, said one officer was wearing a construction safety vest while carrying a rifle.“We need to have better transparency to understand who we’re dealing with, because anybody in the street can just put on a vest and pull out a gun and claim to be ICE,” he said.“I feel like regardless if you’re left or right, we should understand that this shouldn’t be happening.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Psychology says children who ask you to repeat a silly word again and again may be enjoying more than the joke
articles.summary: There is a moment many parents will recognise.
articles.body: There is a moment many parents will recognise. You accidentally call a spoon a “spoonasaurus”, give a funny name to your child’s favourite toy, or say a completely nonsensical word in a silly voice. Your child bursts out laughing and asks you to say it again. You oblige. They laugh harder. Before long, the same word has been repeated 15 times, and you are beginning to wonder what could possibly be so funny about it.For adults, the joke may have run its course after the first few repetitions. For a young child, however, the fun may lie in much more than the word itself. There is the anticipation of hearing it again, the pleasure of knowing what comes next, and the excitement of sharing a moment that makes both of you laugh.This everyday interaction offers a small window into how children experience humour, communicate with others and learn to participate in playful social exchanges. The word may be silly, but the experience surrounding it is not necessarily trivial.Why does the same silly word remain funny?One explanation lies in the way children learn to recognise and appreciate humour. A word becomes amusing not only because of what it means, but also because it sounds unexpected, breaks an established pattern or is delivered in an unusual way.A parent who calls a cat a “fluffy potato” is deliberately mixing things that do not ordinarily belong together. A toddler may not be able to explain why the phrase is funny, but can still enjoy the surprise.Research published in the journal Developmental Psychology by Thomas R. Shultz and Frances Horibe examined how children aged six, eight, 10 and 12 understood verbal jokes. The study found age-related differences in how children appreciated unexpected elements in jokes and how well they understood the resolution that made those jokes meaningful.The findings suggest that recognising humour develops with age and that children do not necessarily process jokes in the same way adults do. For younger children, the unexpected element itself can be particularly appealing.This helps explain why a made-up word, a deliberately wrong label or an exaggerated sound can entertain a child long after an adult has stopped finding it amusing. The child may be enjoying the sound, the surprise or the playful departure from what is normally expected.However, this does not mean that every child who repeats a funny word is consciously analysing a joke. Their enjoyment may be much simpler: something sounds funny, a trusted adult says it, and the experience feels good enough to repeat.The joke may be familiar, but the anticipation is still excitingThere is another reason children may keep asking for the same word: they know what is coming, and they want to experience it again.Adults often associate humour with novelty. Once we know the punchline, the surprise can disappear. Young children, however, may enjoy the entire sequence of a playful exchange, including the familiar sound, the parent's exaggerated expression and the laughter that follows.Think of a parent who says “chocolate” in a squeaky voice every time a child asks for a treat. Soon, the child may start requesting the word before the treat itself. They may even begin laughing in anticipation.The appeal is no longer limited to the original joke. It has become a little ritual between parent and child.A 2025 study published in the journal Social Development, titled Can You Make Me Laugh? Toddlers’ and Parents’ Shared Positive Expressions in Playful Interactions, examined playful interactions involving 80 parent–toddler pairs, with the toddlers aged around 30 months.Researchers observed smiles and laughter during play and found that positive expressions were shared between parents and children. Both could initiate these expressions, and the intensity of their smiling and laughter was positively associated.The study does not specifically establish why children request repeated silly words. It does, however, offer evidence that laughter during early childhood is a shared, interactive experience rather than simply an individual reaction to something funny.When a child asks for the same word again, they may therefore be asking to recreate an enjoyable interaction. The parent’s voice, facial expression and response are all part of what makes the moment work.Repeating the word can also become a game of connectionFor a young child, asking a parent to repeat a silly word is also a way of taking an active role in a conversation.Instead of merely listening to an adult, the child makes a request, watches the response and decides whether the exchange should continue. The parent follows the child's lead, and the child learns that their words can influence what happens next.This is an important feature of early communication. Conversations are not just about learning the meanings of words; they also involve taking turns, responding to another person and expressing what we want.Research on early language development has examined how parents' speech and repetition relate to children's language abilities. A 2020 study in the Journal of Experimental Child Psychology, for example, explored parental repetition during interactions with two-year-olds and its association with vocabulary at age four.The study involved 21 families. Although its findings were limited and did not establish a general causal effect of repetition, the researchers reported a positive association between fathers' repetition of children's utterances at age two and children's vocabulary diversity at age four.This research was not about silly words or humour, so it cannot prove that repeating a funny phrase improves a child's vocabulary. It does, however, illustrate why repeated exchanges between parents and children are worth paying attention to.When a child requests a word again, a parent can respond, pause for the child's reaction and allow the child to initiate the next turn. These small exchanges give children opportunities to communicate their preferences and participate in a shared activity.The important part is not how many times the word is repeated. It is that the child is engaged in an interaction in which their contribution matters.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. articles.title: Britain rebuilt 3.5 miles of the A46 using 17,432 tonnes of material from the old road; the project cut its carbon footprint by 23%
articles.summary: Contractors resurfacing the A46 Warwick Bypass recycled 56% of the materials from the old road back into the new one, cutting the scheme's carbon
articles.body: Contractors resurfacing the A46 Warwick Bypass recycled 56% of the materials from the old road back into the new one, cutting the scheme's carbon footprint by 23%, according to a National Highways press release published on 17 November 2021. According to a National Highways press release, some 17,432 tons of material were reused and saved from landfill across 3.5 miles of the northbound carriageway between Sherbourne roundabout and the Leek Wootton roundabout. Kier led the project on behalf of National Highways and recruited Aggregate Industries to carry out the resurfacing. The work, which ran between late July and September, saved around 82,000 road miles.How did the A46 project cut its carbon footprint by 23%Kier led the project on behalf of National Highways and recruited Aggregate Industries (AI) to carry out the resurfacing. It says the scheme ran between late July and September. Any material not used on the scheme was recycled back into the road network through other projects.Kier Managing Director Scott Cooper is quoted as saying this was the first time Foamix had been used on this type of road on the Area 9 Strategic Road Network. He said the work showed that innovation and collaboration across the value chain are needed for Kier and its partners to reach their net zero ambition. AI's National Technical Manager, Neil Leake, said good collaboration and an innovative approach were at the heart of the scheme. He added that the team had to overcome significant challenges to deliver on time while still meeting its low-carbon goal.How was tar-bound material from the old A46 safely recycledMuch of the material in the lower levels of the road contained tar, which is classed as carcinogenic, meaning it has the potential to cause cancer. Material of this kind must be dealt with as hazardous waste and disposed of at a licensed waste processing facility. The release says, however, that tar-bound material can be safely recycled and encapsulated back into the pavement layers by processing and re-mixing it.Kier and AI devised a low-carbon pavement solution for the project. According to the release, they found the greenest and most cost-effective approach was to recycle the existing carriageway material, which reduced the amount that would otherwise have gone to landfill. The old layers of road were recycled into the new carriageway using AI's ex situ cold recycled Foamix asphalt.How does Foamix reduce asphalt fumesFoamix is a fully cold process that can be laid and compacted at a much safer ambient temperature. This reduces the asphalt fumes on site to which workers are exposed. The material was mixed on site to minimise vehicle movements and reduce the scheme's carbon footprint. Using recycled material also meant less raw material was needed for the works. Together with the avoided trips to the waste site, this meant around 82,000 road miles were saved on the scheme.The project sits within National Highways' wider net zero carbon plan. Project Manager Ryan Davies said the organisation has committed to "rapidly cut carbon from road construction, maintenance and operations". He added that the support of the supply chain is a vital part of meeting its objectives. The release says the plan has three key commitments: net zero for National Highways' own operations by 2030, net zero road maintenance and construction by 2040, and support for net zero carbon travel on its roads by 2050.You use AI every day. articles.title: As US government presents Science medals, Elon Musk shares 'congratulations message' for Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, Michael Dell and Satya Nadella
articles.summary: US government awarded several tech executives with the country’s highest honours for scientific and technological achievements.
articles.body: US government awarded several tech executives with the country’s highest honours for scientific and technological achievements. President Donald Trump presented the National Medal of Science to Google’s co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su, and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, while the National Medal of Technology and Innovation was awarded to Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Elon Musk shared a congratulatory message to fellow recipients on X.“Congratulations to Sergey, Jensen, Lisa, Michael and Satya!,” Musk wrote, replying to a video of the award ceremony event shared by the Official White House Rapid Response team.White House presents science medalsThe medals were presented at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit. In a official press release, the White House said “Since 1963, the President of the United States has bestowed the National Medal of Science on those deserving of special recognition for their outstanding contributions to science in service of the United States”. White the National Medal of Technology and Innovation was first awarded in 1985. It has recognized American innovators whose vision, intellect, creativity, and determination have strengthened America’s economy and improved our quality of life.“Each of these medalists has transformed their field or industry, laying the foundations for technologies we already can barely imagine living without,” said Michael Kratsios, Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “While we in government work to deliver the efforts a New Golden Age of Science will require, we know that scientific progress and technological innovation depend on the insight and character of individuals. Innovators like these six awardees are the architects of the future.”The recipients are listed below.Recipients of the National Medal of ScienceElon Musk – “For engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale that have pushed the frontiers of space exploration, intelligent systems, communications, and beyond, renewing American technological leadership and opening a new chapter in American manufacturing.”Sergey Brin – “For the development of foundational algorithms for information retrieval and data processing that revolutionized how the world accesses information across science, commerce, and in the course of everyday life.”Jensen Huang – “For advancing the graphics processing unit into a general-purpose computing architecture through innovations in processor design and software, transforming massively parallel computation and powering breakthroughs in scientific computing and super intelligence.”Lisa Su – “For a lifetime of leadership in semiconductor engineering and high-performance computing through innovations in processor architecture and chiplet-based integration that powered the world’s first exascale supercomputer and opened new frontiers in computational performance.”Recipients of the National Medal of Technology and InnovationMichael Dell – “For advancing a vision of widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing; for his technical and business management skills building a worldwide technology company; and for his support for the next generation of American scientists, engineers, and technologists.”Satya Nadella – “For his transformative leadership of a critical American technology company, which led to its rejuvenation for a new era of cloud computing, and for his construction of the hyperscale infrastructure that enabled the training and global deployment of American super intelligence.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Jeff Bezos may have just told Americans, stop 'hating' AI, it may make '3-day work week' possible
articles.summary: Jeff Bezos believes that AI can help you support your family while working three days a week.
articles.body: Jeff Bezos believes that AI can help you support your family while working three days a week. In an interview with Fox News recently, the Amazon founder told host Bret Baier he believes AI’s productivity gains could let some people decide, “I can support my family by working three days a week.” Bezos further claimed that in families where both partners work, one person may choose to stop working if they no longer need a second income. While Jeff Bezos did not explain how this could happen, he backed the argument by stating that AI may lead to labor shortages rather than large-scale job losses.Jeff Bezos blames rapid hiring during covid-19 for recent job cuts at AmazonDuring the interview, Jeff Bezos stated that he does not believe that AI will result in job cuts. A “lot of smart people are prognosticating” AI-driven job losses, Bezos said adding “I just happen to disagree with those smart people.”When the host pointed at nearly 30,000 job cuts at Amazon in the last 12 months, Jeff Bezos blamed the company’s hiring spree and its rapid headcount growth after the Covid-19 pandemic.What Jeff Bezos said about the AI bubbleHost Bret Baier also asked Jeff Bezos about his comments that AI was kind of an “industrial bubble” that is “good.”The billionaire replied saying: “What happens in these industrial bubbles…speculators can lose money because they’re investing in all of these things. But the inventions don’t disappear when the bubble pops.”Asked if the world was witnessing a bubble right now, Jeff Bezos replied: “It’s very hard to know. What I do know is the technology is real.” He further argued that a bubble can be good for society, if not investors, because it allows every idea to be funded.Jeff Bezos on AI being renamed as ’SI’Recently, President Donald Trump rebranded artificial intelligence, AI to super intelligence, SI. Bezos said that he like SI because “artificial is not a very flattering thing…Nobody wants an artificial sweetener or artificial flavoring. Artificial sort of means fake.”You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘The Orange Plague’: Why a golden, naked Trump is sitting on another man
articles.summary: A 2.6-metre-tall statue of US president Donald Trump, naked and coated in 23-karat gold leaf, has been installed inside the European parliament in
articles.body: A 2.6-metre-tall statue of US president Donald Trump, naked and coated in 23-karat gold leaf, has been installed inside the European parliament in Strasbourg, France.Titled ‘The Orange Plague’, the sculpture by Danish artist Jens Galschiøt depicts Trump sitting on the shoulders of a frail, smaller man, with his thighs and sagging belly wrapped around the man’s head. Trump holds a golf club in one hand and the scales of justice in the other. The work is also known as the “King of Injustice”.The sculpture is a satirical critique of what Galschiøt sees as Trump’s threats to the environment, international cooperation and the rules-based world order. The artist has said the US president is destroying the causes and institutions he believes in, including efforts to tackle climate change. The work also questions how political power is exercised and how its consequences are borne by those with less power.What does the statue symbolise?The smaller man beneath Trump represents the burden imposed by the powerful on the less powerful.A plaque at the base of the sculpture captures the imbalance through the words: “I am sitting on the back of a man. He is sinking under my burden. I will do anything to help him. Except step down from his back.”The imagery suggests a leader who claims to help others while continuing to place the weight of his power and decisions on them.The golf club and scales of justice add to the political satire, juxtaposing Trump’s personal image with the idea of justice. Its gold finish is also a deliberate choice: Galschiøt has pointed to Trump’s fondness for gold, saying he believes the president might even like the sculpture.Why is Trump depicted naked?Galschiøt has said the sculpture draws inspiration from Danish author Hans Christian Andersen’s fairy tale ‘The Emperor’s New Clothes’, in which a vain emperor parades through his city naked while those around him pretend he is wearing magnificent clothes.This is also not the first Trump sculpture to depict Trump naked based on a correlation with the fairy tale, a previous series of statues displayed across the US by an artist collective was also titled, ‘The Emperor Has No Balls’.By depicting Trump naked, Galschiøt seeks to ridicule the president and strip away the image of authority surrounding him. “Dictators don’t like you laughing at them,” the artist said, explaining the thinking behind the work.Galschiøt is known for provocative political art. His best-known works include the Pillar of Shame, a memorial to victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre that was controversially removed from a Hong Kong university in 2021. He has drawn a parallel between the two works, saying both concern the relationship between the powerful and the powerless.Why has the statue been installed at the European Parliament?The exhibition was sponsored by Danish politician Per Clausen, a member of the European parliament’s left-wing group, The Left. Members of the European Parliament are entitled to sponsor cultural events and exhibitions on parliamentary premises, subject to approval by officials. The sculpture’s installation therefore does not amount to an official endorsement of its message by the European Union.Clausen said he wanted to encourage debate about how power is used around the world and how Europe can protect its interests without becoming dependent on Trump. He defended the exhibition as an opportunity to display work that not everyone might agree with.Galschiøt, who had feared the application would be rejected, viewed the approval as an opportunity to bring criticism of Trump into the European Parliament. He said many Europeans regard the US president’s conduct as a serious problem, even if they recognise that he is the leader of an important ally.Where else has ‘The Orange Plague’ been displayed?The sculpture has previously been displayed at the Munich Security Conference and the COP30 United Nations climate conference in Belém, Brazil, in November 2025. It was also shown at demonstrations in Copenhagen earlier in 2026 calling for Greenland to be protected from US ambitions.The Strasbourg installation was accompanied by 3D-printed miniature versions of the sculpture, distributed to visitors as “protest tokens”. The artist has said he produced around 20,000 miniatures for distribution to visitors and European Parliament staff.The temporary exhibition in Strasbourg is expected to remain on display until Thursday. Galschiøt plans to exhibit the sculpture again at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, next month. Trump has not publicly commented on the artwork.You use AI every day. articles.title: CJP protest: What’s open and what’s closed in Delhi on October 10
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi will see restrictions on retail liquor sales and cancellations of several Mail and Express trains on October 10 amid planned protests by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi will see restrictions on retail liquor sales and cancellations of several Mail and Express trains on October 10 amid planned protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Left groups and student outfits of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protests are also aimed at seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police have stepped up security and outreach efforts across the city, urging residents, students and young people to avoid activities that could disrupt public order.Here is a look at what will remain open and what will be closed in Delhi on October 10.What will be closed1. All retail liquor storesAll retail liquor outlets across Delhi will remain closed on October 9 and 10 following an order issued by the excise department on October 8.The closure applies to retail liquor vends operating under specified licence categories, including outlets selling Indian liquor, foreign liquor and country liquor, as well as certain outlets in malls.The excise department said the decision was taken as a preventive measure to maintain public order in view of the prevailing situation and inputs received from Delhi Police.However, liquor sales at licensed restaurants, bars and clubs will continue as usual, an official clarified.2. Several Mail and Express trainsIndian Railways has ordered the cancellation of several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10.According to a railway order issued on October 9, trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on October 9 and scheduled to reach either of the two stations during the specified period on October 10 will be cancelled at source.The decision was taken due to the possibility of severe road traffic congestion around the two railway stations. Railway officials have not confirmed whether the cancellations are directly linked to the planned protests.3. Entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations may be closedDelhi Police have asked DMRC to close entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9pm on October 9 and continue the restrictions on October 10 until the situation normalises. Train frequency at these stations may also be reduced in view of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations. Passengers are advised to check DMRC updates before travelling.What will remain open1. Licensed restaurants, bars and clubsWhile retail liquor shops will remain shut, licensed restaurants, bars and clubs in Delhi will continue to serve liquor as usual, according to an excise department official.2. Other regular servicesNo blanket closure of other regular public services or commercial establishments has been announced in the information available. Residents should check for specific advisories before travelling or making plans.Police step up security ahead of protestsDelhi Police have warned against the proposed CJP protest on October 10, stating that Section 163 is in force in the national capital and any gathering in violation of the restrictions would be considered illegal.Police teams have contacted market welfare associations, resident welfare associations and Aman committees in several areas, asking them to counsel people against participating in activities that could disturb public order.Sources said police were also checking hotels for last-minute bookings and monitoring railway stations and other transit points. Officers were approaching groups gathered at these locations to inquire about their plans.The protests have been called over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise, with demonstrators also demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A 21-year-old Tennessee moviegoer noticed an 80-year-old AMC usher emptying trash after a screening and hoped a TikTok fundraiser might bring in $500; strangers donated more than $146,000 in less than 24 hours
articles.summary: A 21-year-old woman in Tennessee, United States raised more than $146,000 in less than 24 hours for an 80-year-old cinema worker after noticing her
articles.body: A 21-year-old woman in Tennessee, United States raised more than $146,000 in less than 24 hours for an 80-year-old cinema worker after noticing her cleaning up rubbish at an AMC theatre. What began as a TikTok video and a small fundraising effort soon attracted thousands of people online, with donations far exceeding the $500 the young woman had initially hoped to collect.According to WVLT, Brooklyn Green had gone to watch a film with her grandparents at the AMC theatre in Maryville, Tennessee, when she noticed an elderly employee pushing a cleaning cart and emptying rubbish. The woman was working hard, and Green decided to record a short video of her.“I just saw her work ethic. She was just working really hard,” Green told WVLT. She later posted the video on TikTok and created a GoFundMe campaign to help the worker, hoping she could eventually enjoy retirement.Green initially expected that friends and family might contribute around $500. Instead, the video spread rapidly, and donations crossed $100,000 within the first day. The total eventually reached approximately $146,000 before Green returned to the theatre to surprise the woman.Mary, the 80-year-old cinema workerAfter launching the fundraiser, Green returned to the theatre to find the elderly employee. However, the woman was not working that day. Green spoke to a manager and learnt that her name was Mary.According to the report, Mary had worked in theatres for more than 45 years. Managers told Green that she enjoyed her job and did not want to stop working. They said Mary was concerned that things might go downhill for her if she stopped working at her age.Green also learnt that Mary regularly helped other people. According to the information shared with her, Mary supported her church and people experiencing homelessness.Her willingness to help others became another reason Green wanted the fundraising effort to succeed. Green recalled a conversation with Mary about the people she supported.“She told me that she helps a mother and child and some of the homeless, and I told her that it comes back tenfold,” Green said.Mixed reactions to fundraiserAs the TikTok video gained attention, Green began sharing updates about the fundraising campaign. In one update, she explained that Mary was unaware of the video and the money being collected for her.Green also told followers that Mary might not want to accept the donations. According to the manager, Mary was reluctant to stop working, and Green acknowledged that the elderly woman might choose to give the money to other people or charities.The possibility prompted criticism from some social media users. They questioned whether the donations should be returned if Mary did not want the money or decided against retirement.Green responded by making it clear that Mary would have complete control over the funds. "Guys, I said she will decide regardless what to do with the donations. If she decides to give it to a charity or whatever then that is her decision. She is getting every penny, deep breaths lol," Green wrote.She also acknowledged that some people had criticised her for starting the campaign without first speaking to Mary about retirement. "I have gotten a lot of support, but also a lot of backlash for assuming she wants to retire, as well as her not being aware that I was doing this," Green told Storyful, according to CBS News.Mary reacts to fundraiserDespite the criticism, Green continued with her plan to meet Mary and personally tell her about the donations. Green eventually returned to the AMC theatre while Mary was working and surprised her with news of the fundraising campaign.By then, donations had reached approximately $146,000. Green showed Mary the amount on a tablet, revealing how much money strangers had contributed after watching the TikTok video.Mary was overwhelmed by the response and thanked everyone who had donated.“Thank you so very much to all the wonderful people that have donated money. I’m overwhelmed and certainly blessed by the Lord and you wonderful people,” Mary told WVLT.Following the surprise, Mary asked for the GoFundMe campaign to be paused. She said she had already received more than she could ask for. Meanwhile, Green has decided she will work on other projects intended to support more people.You use AI every day. articles.title: Can a warship become a mini aircraft carrier? India, US are testing two different answers
articles.summary: The idea of turning a warship to a miniature aircraft carrier is moving from concept to contract, with India and the United States both building shipborne
articles.body: The idea of turning a warship to a miniature aircraft carrier is moving from concept to contract, with India and the United States both building shipborne drone capabilities, though at very different ends of the spectrum. Unmanned aircraft that can take off from a moving deck are changing what a warship can see, and in the American case, what it can strike.India's effort is the Naval Shipborne Unmanned Aerial System programme. After the Defence Acquisition Council cleared it in July 2026, the Navy issued an industry notice to move the acquisition forward, with the process meant to be completed by January 31, 2027. The Navy plans to buy around 40 systems for warships longer than 100 metres, each originally envisaged as two unmanned aircraft, a primary control station and a standby control station. The requirement was first outlined through a Request for Information in 2022.The drones will mainly handle intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, tracking suspicious vessels and feeding real-time imagery and sensor data to a warship's command centre. They are also expected to support anti-piracy, counter-terrorism, search-and-rescue and battle damage assessment tasks. Electro-optical and infrared sensors will allow imaging by day and detection at night, while radar and electronic intelligence payloads could pick up radar emissions and communications signals. Compared with helicopters, drones can stay airborne longer at lower operating cost, letting a ship watch a larger area and react faster, and their data can feed combat management systems.The category of the procurement seeks at least 60% indigenous content and at least 50% of materials, components and software must be made in India. Operating drones from a pitching deck is not easy, with strong winds, saltwater corrosion, secure data links and contested electronic environments among the challenges. Indian conglomerate JSW Group and US firm Sheild AI have partnered to make the V-Bat runway-independent drone in India, this unmanned system has demonstrated its naval applications.The American effort aims much higher. Shield AI's X-BAT is billed as an AI-piloted, vertical takeoff and landing fighter-class aircraft that needs no runway. It has a 39-foot wingspan, a range of 2,000 nautical miles and a ceiling above 50,000 feet, and is run by the company's Hivemind AI pilot, which can carry out strike, electronic warfare and surveillance missions even where GPS and communications are jammed. Shield AI says the first prototypes are due by the end of this month, with flight testing before the year ends and full production planned for 2029.The US Navy has now executed a $150 million modification to its existing agreement with the company, funded through a Pentagon exportability programme, with Shield AI matching it from its own capital. That follows a $50 million Navy investment earlier this year, made with the Defense Innovation Unit under the Runway Independent Maritime Expeditionary Strike effort, bringing the combined total to $400 million.The two programmes sit at opposite ends. India wants eyes in the sky for its escorts, while Washington is betting on drones that can fight from ships without a flight deck. Both rest on the same logic, that a warship need not be a carrier to project air power.

articles.title: ‘Cover it from a distance’: Delhi Police releases statement after accusations of journalists being placed under house arrest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Additional DCP New Delhi Manjeet Sheoran on Friday urged journalists to maintain a distance from protesters while covering demonstrations.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Additional DCP New Delhi Manjeet Sheoran on Friday urged journalists to maintain a distance from protesters while covering demonstrations. He alleged that some media personnel join protests and obstruct police work."Some protestors come one day as a journalist and come the other day as a protestor. We keep appealing to them that you keep a little distance from the protestors, cover it from a distance. But still, they come in between and put obstacles in our work," Sheoran said."Journalism has its role; journalism is not to be rolled," Delhi police said in a post on X.This comes amid allegations that people are being forcibly removed from trains, picked up from their homes and taken to undisclosed locations to prevent them from joining protests."People are being dragged off trains, forcibly picked up from their homes and taken to unknown locations. Even mosques are reportedly being asked to tell people not to join the protests. Is this what the police are meant to do in a democracy? The police are acting like BJP’s political machinery, not an independent force meant to protect citizens and uphold the law. DEMOCRACY IS UNDER ATTACK!" AISA chief Neha Bora said in a post on XThe Delhi Police also has transferred complaints filed by three women journalists alleging sexual harassment and manhandling by police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 3 to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further investigation.Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said the three women, who identified themselves as journalists, lodged a complaint around 6 pm, alleging that they had been manhandled by police officers and staff during their detention.“Their complaint has been registered, medical examinations have been conducted, and the matter has been referred to the Crime Branch,” Yadav said.The complaints were received by the New Delhi district police amid what it described as an “emergent law and order situation” during the protest.Meanwhile, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Thursday took suo motu cognisance of a media report alleging that three women journalists were subjected to sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel during the protest.The Commission said the allegations, if true, raised serious concerns over human rights violations. articles.title: A Miami airport passenger had an ‘unexplained bulge’; officers found 10 live birds hidden in his underwear
articles.summary: A Miami International Airport passenger returning from Cuba was arrested after US Customs and Border Protection officers found 10 live birds concealed in
articles.body: A Miami International Airport passenger returning from Cuba was arrested after US Customs and Border Protection officers found 10 live birds concealed in plastic tubes sewn into his underwear. Alberto Hernandez Castillo, 40, a Cuban national and permanent resident of the US, arrived from Havana on October 4 aboard World Atlantic Flight 503 and was selected for a secondary inspection. According to a federal criminal complaint, Castillo declared that he was not bringing animals or wildlife into the US. Officers searching his luggage found no contraband, but then noticed an “unexplained bulge” around his waist and pelvic area. A subsequent pat-down allegedly uncovered six concealed tubes containing the birds.‘Unexplained bulge’ raises suspicion at Miami airportDuring the secondary inspection, Castillo reportedly told officers that he had travelled to Cuba to visit family and was carrying a carry-on bag and a fanny pack. He signed a Customs Entry Declaration in which he answered “No” when asked whether he was bringing animals or wildlife into the country, according to the complaint.Officers searched his belongings but found nothing unusual. During further questioning, however, they noticed what the complaint described as an “unexplained bulge” at the front of his waist and pelvis. Officers also reported that he appeared nervous. They then took him to a secure area for a pat-down.Six tubes were sewn into his underwearThe pat-down allegedly revealed six clear cylindrical plastic containers wrapped in tape and concealed inside black pockets sewn into Castillo's underwear. The openings of the containers had black mesh attached to allow airflow.Inside the containers were 10 live birds. Investigators preliminarily identified eight of them as yellow-faced grassquits (Tiaris olivaceus) and two as blue grosbeaks (Passerina caerulea). Several of the birds were subsequently placed in a cage after being removed from the containers, according to ABC News.Eight yellow-faced grassquits and two blue grosbeaksThe eight yellow-faced grassquits are small seed-eating birds found across parts of Central America, South America and the Caribbean, including Cuba. The two blue grosbeaks are North American songbirds. The species were identified preliminarily by investigators following the discovery at the airport.CBS Miami reported that blue grosbeaks are protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918, meaning their transport requires the appropriate authorisation. Both species have also been associated with illegal bird trafficking, including trade for pets and singing competitions.He said the birds were for “personal use”After the birds were discovered, Castillo allegedly told officers that they were for his “personal use”, according to the criminal complaint. He then invoked his right to remain silent.Federal investigators said Castillo did not have the documentation required to legally import the birds into the US and had not obtained the necessary clearance from the US Fish and Wildlife Service. He was subsequently charged with smuggling goods into the United States.Following his arrest, Castillo appeared in federal court in Miami and was released on a $25,000 personal surety bond. His arraignment is scheduled for October 26, 2026.The US Fish and Wildlife Service is investigating the incident. The status of the 10 birds was not immediately clear in the latest reports.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
